narrative:
The model predicts you have a 12% chance of failing your final year, which is low but enough for the school to require you to take remedial courses as a precaution.

The three factors that most influenced this decision were your reason for choosing the school, your clean record of past failures, and your strong desire to pursue higher education. Surprisingly, these elements pushed the prediction in different directions. Wanting to continue into higher education was a strong positive force, pulling the outcome toward passing because nearly every student who shares this ambition succeeds. Your lack of any previous class failures also helped your case, as students with zero past failures tend to perform better overall.

However, your main reason for selecting this school—its reputation—worked against you. Among students who passed, choosing the school for its reputation is less common than choosing it for the specific course offered. This factor became the most influential one and ultimately tipped the balance enough for the model to flag a risk of failure.

To improve, focus on turning your ambition for higher education into concrete daily habits. Even though you already study 2 to 5 hours weekly (more than many who pass), consider increasing this and reducing your very high frequency of going out with friends. These small adjustments could strengthen the positive signals the model already sees in you and help ensure you pass comfortably.
